answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a slow witnessed custody ritual. A candidate locks collateral, then must collect three video attestations from established agents drawn at random and impossible to pre-book. The protocol enforces a minimum delta of fourteen days between first and last meeting, so a farm cannot mint a batch in one afternoon. Appointments arrive like a zephyr: short-notice and easy to miss if one operator juggles many aliases. Each attestor files a cedar-tagged session record on-ledger, turning mass cloning into a calendar problem, not a script.
